title: Jensen Huang’s departure blasts big hole in AI startup funding, VCs and founders say
lede: Founders and investors tell TechCrunch that Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia removes one of AI startups' largest backers, and expect smaller checks and lower valuations under a more cautious interim CEO.

points: PitchBook counts Nvidia in 105 funding rounds this year, often as the largest investor.
Investors say Huang personally drove most big startup bets; interim CEO Colette Kress is described as far more conservative.
The biggest bets went to neoclouds, inference providers and open-weight labs, including CoreWeave, Crusoe, Mistral AI and Reflection AI.
One VC says infrastructure startups often raised half their GPU budget from Nvidia at valuations of $1 billion or more, which reassured other investors.
Some expect Google, Amazon, Microsoft or AMD to back mature startups, but doubt they will fund pre-revenue infrastructure the same way.

sections.text: The neocloud, inference and open-weight layer many AI builders rely on was largely bankrolled by Nvidia; slower funding there could thin that market, while rival chips and clouds get more room to court startups.
